description: System design is a plan for how the parts of an app work together. Think of planning a school library: people need to find books, borrow them, and return them safely. In 30 lessons, follow one request, choose useful data, estimate busy times, and learn what to do when a part stops working. Explore databases, caches, load balancers, queues, backups, and security with small examples. Then work through plans for a library, short links, chat, a news feed, and file uploads. Clear diagrams and practice questions help you explain each choice. You can read the whole course without a cloud account. Small JavaScript and SQLite models run in the playground.
versionNote: Design plans and small browser models. These examples explain ideas; they do not create real servers, cloud services, or user accounts.
whatYouWillLearn: Turn a goal into clear requirements and a small first design
Follow a request through an API and a database
Estimate demand and explain speed, capacity, and cost tradeoffs
Use caches, copies, partitions, and queues for the right reasons
Plan for retries, failures, backups, and private data
Work through five app designs and explain your choices
learningObjectives: Draw a request flow and give every part a clear job
Choose data and API rules that fit the problem
Check calculations with units and state your assumptions
Explain a benefit and a cost of each added part
Describe what a person sees when a part fails
Review a design using measurements and small tests

seo.title: System Design Tutorial for Beginners: 30 Clear Lessons
seo.description: Learn system design with simple diagrams, examples, and practice. Explore databases, caching, scaling, reliability, and five worked app designs.
